title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of C6-modified Celastrol derivatives as anti-inflammatory agents targeting the NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Yang, Hao-Ran; Wang, Jun-Xia; Jin, Long-Long; Wang, Qing; Yang, Hui-Ying; Wu, Xian-Fu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究C6修饰的Celastrol衍生物抗炎活性及NF-kappaB通路抑制，分子对接仅针对IKKbeta小分子靶点，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Celastrol is a potent natural anti-inflammatory agent, while systematic exploration of C6 structural modification and its structure-activity relationship (SAR) remains limited. In this study, twenty C6-modified Celastrol derivatives were synthesized via thiol-mediated Michael addition followed by phenolic acetylation. For the first time, the anti-inflammatory activity of all synthesized C6-substituted derivatives were systematically evaluated in an LPS-induced RAW264.7 cell model. Most derivatives retained comparable NO inhibitory activity to Celastrol and significantly higher than Curcumin. Preliminary structure-activity relationship analysis indicated that alkyl substitutions at the C6 position exhibited more potent NO inhibitory activity than aryl, and this effect was influenced by multiple factors, including substituent chain length, steric hindrance, and electronic effects. Among all derivatives, compound 6e exhibited a favorable balance between NO inhibitory activity and cytotoxicity. 6e effectively suppressed the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha and IL-6) and inhibited NF-kappaB signaling by reducing the phosphorylation of IkappaBalpha and p65, as well as downregulating iNOS expression. Molecular docking studies targeting IKKbeta, a key upstream regulator of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, demonstrated that 6e could be favorably accommodated within the active site through multiple stabilizing interactions, providing a structural basis for its inhibitory effects on NF-kappaB signaling pathway. In conclusion, this study provides a systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) insight into C6 modification of Celastrol and highlights this position as a viable site for structural diversification while maintaining anti-inflammatory activity, offering insights for further structural optimization.
abstract_zh: Celastrol是一种强效的天然抗炎剂，然而对其C6位结构修饰及其构效关系（SAR）的系统性探索仍然有限。在本研究中，通过硫醇介导的Michael加成反应及随后的酚乙酰化，合成了二十种C6修饰的Celastrol衍生物。首次在LPS诱导的RAW264.7细胞模型中对所有合成的C6取代衍生物的抗炎活性进行了系统评估。大多数衍生物保持了与Celastrol相当的NO抑制活性，并显著高于Curcumin。初步构效关系分析表明，C6位上的烷基取代比芳基取代表现出更强的NO抑制活性，且该效应受多种因素影响，包括取代基链长、空间位阻和电子效应。在所有衍生物中，化合物6e在NO抑制活性和细胞毒性之间表现出良好的平衡。6e有效抑制了促炎细胞因子（TNF-alpha和IL-6）的产生，并通过减少IkappaBalpha和p65的磷酸化以及下调iNOS表达来抑制NF-kappaB信号通路。针对NF-kappaB信号通路关键上游调控因子IKKbeta的分子对接研究表明，6e可通过多种稳定相互作用被良好地容纳于活性位点内，这为其对NF-kappaB信号通路的抑制作用提供了结构基础。总之，本研究为Celastrol的C6修饰提供了系统的构效关系（SAR）见解，并强调该位点是在保持抗炎活性的同时进行结构多样化的可行位点，为进一步的结构优化提供了启示。
